description: We are a crew of indie developers and space romantics who decided that staying on Earth is boring. For this hackathon, we’ve joined forces to build not just a game, but a real portal to unexplored worlds. Our tech stack is fueled by dark matter, and our ambitions stretch far beyond the Solar System.
summary:
ARES is an interactive platform for Mars exploration and mission planning. It features a 3D visualization of the solar system, a surface atlas based on data from NASA and the U.S. Geological Survey, and a route planner that accounts for terrain, energy consumption, time, and simulated risks.

Users can select a specific area, plot a route with intermediate waypoints, and explore it across a 3D representation of the Martian surface.

Tech stack: JavaScript, Three.js, WebGL, Node.js, and GeoTIFF. The project is intended for research and exploratory purposes, not for controlling actual missions.
details:
ARES — Mars Exploration Atlas is an interactive platform for exploring Mars and planning simulated surface missions. It combines a 3D space experience, orbital imagery, terrain elevation data, climate scenarios, and route optimization in one connected application.

Users begin with a journey from the Milky Way through the Solar System to Mars. They can explore all eight planets, inspect Phobos and Deimos, and switch between a Martian globe and a detailed surface map. The atlas integrates NASA and USGS datasets, allowing users to select coordinates and examine different imagery and environmental layers.

Safe Route Lab helps users plan missions across selected Martian terrain. Users define a starting point, intermediate stops, a destination, and exclusion zones, then configure constraints such as energy reserves, travel time, slope limits, and modeled environmental risks. The planner uses A* and resource-constrained search, with Dijkstra-based verification where applicable. Results include route comparisons, elevation profiles, resource estimates, and exportable mission reports.

3D Terrain Lab lets users inspect selected locations as three-dimensional landscapes built from elevation data. It includes a catalog of named Martian features, custom locations, surface imagery, and route visualization. Routes calculated in Safe Route Lab can be transferred to the 3D viewer and exported in GPX format.

The platform also provides climate scenarios covering temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind, and dust, alongside archived MEDA and REMS observations. These datasets provide context for exploring mission assumptions.

Technology stack: JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, Three.js, WebGL, Canvas 2D, Web Workers, Node.js, and GeoTIFF.js. The backend provides REST APIs, while JSON files and a filesystem cache store datasets and routes.

ARES is designed for research, education, and demonstration. Its route recommendations are optimal only within the selected terrain graph and configured model; they are not operational guidance or a guarantee of safety for real Mars missions.
